annotation.title_clean: Australia's System of Control and applications for Autonomous Weapon Systems
annotation.title_en: Australia's System of Control and applications for Autonomous Weapon Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Australia (Government), submitted to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS
annotation.summary_en: Australian working paper to the CCW GGE on LAWS describing its nine-stage system of control over military weapons, applied to autonomous weapon systems from legal framework through design, Article 36 review, certification, deployment and after-action review. It argues existing international law and internal processes suffice, so no specific ban is needed.
key_provisions_or_claims: A layered nine-stage system of control covers weapons from design to after-action evaluation.
Article 36 weapons review is required before any new weapon, including AWS, enters service.
Existing IHL and national regulation suffice; no specific ban on AWS is needed at this time.
Rules of engagement and targeting directives apply to AWS as to any weapon or operator.
The term 'human control' is considered inadequate as a basis for GGE discussions without common understanding.
